location: Viña del Mar, Chile · Remote worldwide
role: Cloud Architect & Software Engineer · 13+ years · builds the product, runs the platform
summary: Founded Eleva in 2017 for schools that needed staff evaluations they could trust; it won Startup Chile Ignite (generation 4, 2022) and still runs in production. Since 2024 I lead Liquor Cart, which turned on-premise registers and an online store into one system the business runs without a developer. Deployments are pipelines that roll back on their own: Eleva shipped 19 times last month, none failed. I build the product and keep it predictable — usually two jobs, on my systems one.
highlights: Built from zero, still in production: Eleva, a multitenant SaaS for schools, since 2017. One CDK stack class and one config record describe dev, qa and prod, so a new environment is a pull request.
Made delivery predictable: 19 production deploys in 30 days, none failed, a commit live in about nine minutes, and ECS rolls a bad one back itself — every push to main, through three CodePipelines.
Turned audits into a glance: Eleva's ops panel reads the architecture from deployed CloudFormation, checks drift per resource, and every image carries its commit hash.

Designed for safe recovery: one RabbitMQ virtual host per Liquor Cart store; a saga reconciles money with orders — voids, refunds, cancels or completes under idempotent keys; unclear cases go to a person.
Time to update, known by design: an order reaches the broker as it commits and the register once paid, a product is live on the next request once written, a release is budgeted at ten minutes.

experience.title: Lead Software Architect & Full-Stack Engineer
bullets: Led the replacement of a legacy commerce platform with Liquor Cart: registers stay on-premise, the Magento storefront runs in AWS, and the two operate as one system.
Designed the middleware on MassTransit over RabbitMQ (Amazon MQ) and wrote nine of every ten lines of its C#. Each store gets its own virtual host, created at onboarding and deleted at retirement.
Gave the payment saga a clock the broker cannot keep: deadlines live in Postgres, swept every minute. First check two minutes after settlement, then up to four more five minutes apart, then a person.
Made the consumers safe to repeat: transactional outbox and inbox, deterministic message ids, five retries backing off from a second to five minutes, then an error queue an operator can replay.
Put an anti-corruption layer in front of the event-sourced order book: 8 event kinds, wire values frozen so the domain can evolve. An unknown kind is acknowledged and dropped, not retried.

An order is published the moment it commits. The middleware pulls it, acknowledges it back and posts it to the register once paid. A ten-minute cron retries failures and marks rows stalled after thirty.
Replaced manual deployments with CI/CD to AWS: Magento on ECS, Aurora and FSx, defined in CDK and deployed to dev, qa and prod accounts from one trunk, with prod behind a manual approval.
Set the conventions a six-person team ships through and mentored its juniors — 178 pull requests merged, 1,600+ unit tests on every push.

experience.title: Founder & Platform Architect
bullets: Founded Eleva in 2017 and still run it in production: a multitenant SaaS for schools' 360-degree performance evaluations and improvement plans. Startup Chile Ignite winner, generation 4 (2022).
Architected the platform as code with CDK and Projen: a .NET API on ECS Fargate behind API Gateway (no ALB, no NAT to pay for), a 104-component Angular SPA on S3/CloudFront, PostgreSQL 17 on RDS.
Designed the platform to tolerate being off: at 21:00 every weekday ECS scales to zero and RDS stops, and it comes back on request. Cold starts are routine, not incidents.
Built the ops control panel: it renders the architecture from deployed CloudFormation, checks drift per resource, tails logs and approves pipeline gates. New stacks appear in it by convention.

Designed the event-driven domain so tenants stay isolated and results stay auditable: versioned rubrics and scales, a four-stage evaluation lifecycle, and weighted 360° scores that compensate for missing evaluators.
